answer: A DEA registration makes each extra identity pay $888, the three-year practitioner fee; a farm running N fakes pays N×$888 and cannot share it because the DEA issues one number to one practitioner on one state license. A farm reusing one DEA number dies by DEA lookup at 2: the duplicate flags both registrations for investigation. A saffron stamp marks each file in a grove of county records, and a tundra clinic files the same form as a city hospital. A 500-seat farm files 500 registrations, $444,000, before one fake earns.
